name: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis
description: Separate DNA or RNA fragments by size using agarose gel electrophoresis. Adjust agarose percentage based on expected fragment sizes (0.8–1% for 500 bp–10 kb; 2% for <500 bp).
source_note: General educational template based on standard agarose gel electrophoresis protocols.

steps.title: Prepare agarose solution
steps.description: Weigh agarose and dissolve in 1x TAE or TBE running buffer to the desired percentage. 1% gel: 1 g agarose per 100 mL buffer.
steps.notes: Use the same buffer in the gel and the running tank.

steps.title: Melt agarose in microwave
steps.description: Microwave the agarose slurry in short intervals, swirling between pulses, until completely dissolved and the solution is clear with no undissolved particles.
steps.shakingRotation: Swirl every 30 s between microwave pulses
steps.notes: Microwave in 30 s intervals to prevent boiling over. Solution should be completely clear.
steps.warnings: HOT: use oven mitts. Superheating risk — handle with care. Do not seal the flask.

steps.title: Cool and add nucleic acid stain
steps.description: Cool the melted agarose to ~55–60°C (too hot to hold comfortably, but not solidifying). Add the DNA stain and swirl gently to mix.

reagents.name: Nucleic acid stain (SYBR Safe, EtBr, or equivalent)
reagents.notes: e.g., 5 µL of 10,000x SYBR Safe per 100 mL gel

steps.notes: If using EtBr, handle with appropriate PPE (gloves, eye protection). Consider SYBR Safe as a safer alternative.
steps.warnings: Ethidium bromide is a potent mutagen. Use PPE and follow institutional disposal procedures.

steps.title: Pour gel and insert comb
steps.description: Pour the warm agarose into the gel casting tray. Insert the comb(s) at the desired position. Allow the gel to solidify at room temperature.
steps.notes: Avoid bubbles when pouring. The gel is solidified when it turns opaque and firm to the touch.

steps.title: Prepare samples and load gel
steps.description: Remove the comb carefully. Place gel in the electrophoresis tank with 1x running buffer covering the gel. Mix DNA samples with loading dye and load wells. Load DNA ladder in at least one lane.

reagents.name: DNA ladder (size marker)
reagents.notes: Use appropriate size range for your fragments

equipment: Gel electrophoresis tank and power supply
steps.notes: Ensure buffer level is slightly above gel surface. Load samples slowly to avoid mixing between wells.

steps.title: Run gel electrophoresis
steps.description: Run at 80–120 V until loading dye has migrated an appropriate distance. Lower voltage gives better resolution; higher voltage is faster but generates more heat.
steps.notes: Running at 100 V: ~30–45 min for typical DNA separation. Watch the leading dye front.
steps.warnings: Electric shock hazard. Do not open tank while running. Confirm polarity: DNA migrates toward positive (red) electrode.

steps.title: Image gel
steps.description: Image the gel on a UV transilluminator or gel documentation system. Photograph the gel showing DNA bands and ladder.
equipment: UV transilluminator or gel doc system
steps.notes: Minimize UV exposure time to preserve DNA for gel extraction if needed.
steps.warnings: UV radiation is hazardous to eyes and skin. Wear UV-protective face shield or goggles and protective clothing.
